title: The whole Bible in two minutes
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions and its rows of docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: The Bible starts with God. He speaks, and there's a world.
He calls it good. And he makes people in his image, to look after it for him.

scripture.text: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.

lines: Then the first people reach for the one thing God held back. And the damage spreads. Shame. Blame. A murder. A flood. A tower built to reach the sky.
God judges it. And he keeps showing mercy.
So God picks one man, Abraham, and makes him a promise. A people. A land. And a blessing meant for every family on earth.

scripture.text: all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.

lines: Abraham's family grows into a nation, and the nation ends up as slaves in Egypt. God hears them. He spares them by the blood of a lamb and opens a road through the sea.
At Mount Sinai he makes a covenant with them, gives them his law, and has them build a tent so he can live among them.

scripture.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

lines: God gives them the land. But they keep turning away, and each round is worse than the last.
They ask for a king. Saul fails. David loves God and fails badly too. And God promises David a son whose kingdom will never end.

scripture.text: your throne will be established forever.

chapters.kicker: Exile, and promises in the dark
lines: The kingdom splits. The kings lead the people to idols, the prophets call them back, and they won't come. Babylon burns Jerusalem.
But in the dark, the prophets promise a new covenant and a coming king. Some of the exiles come home and rebuild. No son of David sits on the throne. The Old Testament ends looking ahead.

scripture.text: I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.

lines: Then God keeps his promises in person. Jesus says God's kingdom has come near. He heals, he forgives, and he speaks with an authority that belongs to God alone.
He dies on a Roman cross at Passover, carrying the sin of the world. And on the third day God raises him bodily from the dead.

scripture.text: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures

lines: Fifty days later the Spirit comes. The church starts in Jerusalem and spreads, Jews and Gentiles together, until the news about Jesus reaches Rome.

scripture.text: you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.

lines: And the story ends where it began, with God and his people together. Only now the garden has become a city.
Jesus returns. Death is undone. And God makes his home with people forever.
Behold, I make all things new.

scripture.text: Behold, I make all things new.

lines: That's the whole Bible, from the garden to the city. And you're living somewhere on that road.
titleCard: You're living somewhere on that road.
